children: Investors are likely face a period of higher yields for longer, Vontobel's Christian Hantel says in note. The global bond sell-off continues on the back of renewed tensions between the U.S. and Iran and rising oil prices as a result, the portfolio manager says. Investors also seem to digest Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's speech at the Jackson Hole symposium and his more hawkish tone, he says. "As Warsh was very firm on bringing down inflation to the 2% target, he also emphasized that there could be more work to do to ultimately achieve this goal," he says. "So now we are likely to live with higher yields for longer." (emese.bartha@wsj.com)
